parole.significato: Forms primarily momentane verbs.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-altadak, from Proto-Finno-Ugric [Term?].

parole.significato: Forms some adjectives.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-as, a variant of *-s (adjective-forming suffix), from Proto-Finno-Ugric *-s.

parole.significato: Marker of conditional mood in verbs.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-ici- (related to Karelian -si- and Veps -isi-), from Proto-Finno-Ugric *-ńće-j, *-nśe-j; derived from the same ending as in -ista (see *-istak).

parole.significato: Forms diminutive nouns.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-kka, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *-kka (compare Erzya -ка (-ka), Hungarian -ka).

parole.significato: Forms nouns that signify a place, such as an abode, a house, a land of, a farm, etc.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-la, from Proto-Finno-Ugric [Term?]. Cognate with Estonian -la.

parole.significato: Forms comparative adjectives.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-mpi, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *-mpa. Cognate with Hungarian -bb and the element -mb- in Moksha сембе (sembe, “all”) and Erzya омбо (ombo, “other”), томбале (tombale, “beyond”).

parole.significato: Forms action nouns from certain verbs, mainly related to sound, whose first infinitive ends in -sta.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-na, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *-na.

parole.significato: Forms nouns or adjectives, mostly from nominal stems.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-ra, from Proto-Finno-Ugric [Term?].

parole.significato: Forms frequentative verbs, chiefly from bisyllabic stems.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-skëldak, initial component from Proto-Finno-Ugric *-śk- and the latter equivalent to -ella.

parole.significato: the string in the upper or lower edge of a fishing net or seine; line in a gillnet
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *aina (compare Estonian ain), possibly from Proto-Finno-Ugric *ajna.

parole.significato: bathtub, tub (large container for holding water in which a person may bathe)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *ammëh, derived from Proto-Finno-Ugric *amma- (compare Erzya амолямс (amoľams), Eastern Mansi [script needed] (ūmp)).

parole.significato: steppe; flat, vast, temperate but relatively dry grassland
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *aro (compare Estonian aru), probably from Proto-Finno-Ugric *arɜ (compare Erzya аразь (araź, “lack”), Northern Khanty [script needed] (wuri), Northern Mansi [script needed] (ūraj)).

parole.significato: to open
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *avait'ak (compare Estonian avama, Veps avaita, Votic avatõ), derived from Proto-Finno-Ugric *aŋa- (compare Hungarian old (“to untie, to solve”), Erzya анксема (anksema, “ice hole”), автемс (avtems, “to open”) (from *aŋta-), Northern Mansi [script needed] (āŋkwi, “to open, to take

parole.significato: batch (quantity of anything produced at one operation)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *erä (compare Estonian ära (“away”)), from Proto-Finno-Ugric *erä (“apart”).

parole.significato: common eider (Somateria mollissima)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *hahka (“gray?”), possibly from Proto-Finno-Ugric *ačka (“gray? white?”). If so, may be related to Erzya ашо (ašo, “white”).

parole.significato: he, she, one, they sg (only of a human being; gender-neutral)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *hän (compare Estonian enda, Veps hän), from Proto-Finno-Ugric *sän (compare Northern Sami son, Erzya сон (son), Komi-Zyrian сійӧ (sijö), Hungarian ő). In practically all dialects (except potentially Ingrian Finnish), se is the most common third-person pronoun for people, and this

parole.significato: waterfall
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *juka, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *juka.

parole.significato: ice (water in solid form)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *jää (compare Estonian jää), from Proto-Finno-Ugric *jäŋe (compare Northern Sami jiekŋa, Erzya эй (ej), Eastern Mari ий (ij), Udmurt йӧ (jö), Northern Mansi я̄ӈк (â̄ňk), Eastern Khanty йӛӈк (jjəṇk), Hungarian jég).

parole.significato: to cool, cool down
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *jähtüdäk, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *jäkše-. Cognate with Erzya экше (ekše), экшемемс (ekšemems).

parole.significato: to touch [with illative] (to physically disturb; to interfere with, molest, or attempt to harm through contact)
parole.testo: Derived from Proto-Finnic *kajadak + -ota, possibly from Proto-Finno-Ugric *kajɜ-.

parole.significato: stump, tree stump
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kanto, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *kënta-w, borrowed from Proto-Indo-Iranian *skandʰás, whence Sanskrit स्कन्ध (skandha). Uralic cognates include Erzya кандо (kando, “block, log”).

parole.significato: bitter, resentful (of a person: feeling bitterness or having a bitter temperament; of events: leaving someone feeling b…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kackëra, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *kačka-.

parole.significato: circle, ring (enclosure, perimeter, a circular arrangement of something)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kehä (compare Estonian keha (“body”)), possibly from Proto-Finno-Ugric *keč(č)ä (compare Northern Sami giessat (“to wrap”), Erzya чи (či, “sun, da”), Eastern Mari кече (keče, “sun, day”), Udmurt киш (kiš, “snare”), Northern Mansi кис (kis, “hoop”)).

parole.significato: A circular or near-circular, usually wooden, rim, edge, wheel or ring.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *keri, probably from Proto-Finno-Ugric *kere.

parole.significato: to beg (for) (request the help of someone, often in the form of money; plead for help)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kerjät'äk, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *kerjä- (“to request”) (compare Hungarian kér).

parole.significato: moth: common clothes moth, Tineola bisselliella
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *koi, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *käjä. Cognate with Estonian koi, Erzya ки (ki).

parole.significato: three
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kolmë(t) (compare Estonian kolm), from Proto-Finno-Ugric *kolme (compare Erzya колмо (kolmo), Northern Khanty хәԯум (həłum), Northern Mansi хӯрум (hūrum), Hungarian három).

parole.significato: hole, dent, groove, nook (hollow place or cavity, especially a small one)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kolo, possibly from Proto-Finno-Ugric *kolɜ.

parole.significato: merganser (duck in the genus Mergus)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *koskëlo, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *kośka.

parole.significato: A traditional conical or hemispherical shelter/hut, possibly with an open fireplace in the middle, usually supported by…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kota (compare Estonian koda), from Proto-Finno-Ugric *kota (compare Erzya кудо (kudo), Hungarian ház).

parole.significato: fist (hollow of the hand)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kopra, possibly from Proto-Finno-Ugric *kopra.

parole.significato: corner (external point where two converging lines meet)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kulma (compare Estonian kulm), possibly from Proto-Finno-Ugric *kulma (“corner of the eye”) (compare Eastern Khanty кулӛм (kuljəm, “temple (of the skull)”)).

parole.significato: to wear (out/thin/down) (e.g. of clothes or parts)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kuludak (compare Estonian kuluma, Livonian ku’llõ), from Proto-Finno-Ugric *kule- (compare Erzya каладомс (kaladoms), Northern Khanty [Term?], Northern Mansi [Term?]).

parole.significato: bubble (spherically contained volume of air or other gas)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kupla (compare Estonian kubel), possibly from Proto-Finno-Ugric *kupla (compare Southern Sami gåbloe (“lung”), Inari Sami koble (“roe pouch”), Eastern Mari кувыл (kuvyl, “bubbles on the water surface, due to rain”), Southern Mansi [script needed] (kɛ̮wl-, “to swim, to float”)).

parole.significato: ravine, flume, gulch, gorge (narrow V-shaped valley, often with water running through)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kuru (compare Estonian kuru), from Proto-Finno-Ugric *kure (compare Komi-Zyrian кыр (kyr), Eastern Mari курык (kuryk), Eastern Khanty кор (kor)).

parole.significato: to spawn
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kutëdak, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *kuďe-.

parole.significato: animal fat, fat, tallow, especially reindeer fat
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kuu, probably from Proto-Finno-Ugric; see the Proto-Finnic entry for details.

parole.significato: to hear (perceive through hearing)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kuuldak (compare Estonian kuulma), from Proto-Finno-Ugric *kuwle- (compare Northern Sami gullat, Moksha кулемс (kulems), Eastern Mari колаш (kolaš), Northern Mansi хӯлуӈкве (hūluňkve), Hungarian hall).

parole.significato: to listen (to)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kundëldak, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *kuntale- (compare Hungarian hall), frequentative of *kunta- (“to hunt, catch”) (compare Erzya verbs кундамс (kundams, “to catch; to grip”) and кунсоломс (kunsoloms, “to listen; to comply, obey”)). The long vowel -uu- is by contamination with kuul

parole.significato: groove, ridge (long, narrow channel or depression)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kurna, possibly from Proto-Finno-Ugric *kurńa.

parole.significato: six
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kuuci (compare Estonian kuus), from Proto-Finno-Ugric *kutte (compare Erzya кото (koto), Northern Khanty хәт (hət), Northern Mansi хо̄т (hōt), Hungarian hat).

parole.significato: to smolder/smoulder (burn with no flame and little smoke)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kütedäk, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *küče-.

parole.significato: hand, arm; an upper limb of a human or certain animals
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *käci (compare Estonian käsi), from Proto-Finno-Ugric *käte (compare Northern Sami giehta, Erzya кедь (keď), Eastern Mari кид (kid), Komi-Zyrian ки (ki), Hungarian kéz).

parole.significato: to calm down, stop being angry [with illative ‘at’], forgive, come around
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *leppüdäk, possibly derived from Proto-Finno-Ugric *leppɜ (“soft”).

parole.significato: bird (animal in the class Aves, having a beaked mouth and usually capable of flight)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *lintu (compare Estonian lind), possibly from Proto-Finno-Ugric *lunta (compare Ter Sami lonnˈt, Northern Mansi лунт (lunt), Hungarian lúd); see the Proto-Finnic entry for more.

parole.significato: left, longer ski
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *lülü, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *lelew. Cognates include Estonian lüli, Komi-Zyrian лолӧд (lolöd) and Northern Khanty лӑл (lăl).

parole.significato: to hit, strike, knock
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *löödäk (compare Estonian lööma), from Proto-Finno-Ugric *lewe- (“to throw”) (compare Eastern Mari лӱяш (lüjaš), Komi-Zyrian лыйны (lyjny, “to throw, to shoot”), Northern Mansi лыӈкве (lyňkve), Hungarian lő (“to shoot”), and possibly Erzya ледемс (ledems, “to mow, cut; shoot”)).

parole.significato: flap (anything broad and flexible that hangs loose, or that is attached by one side or end and is easily moved)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *läppä (compare Karelian läppä), possibly from Proto-Finno-Ugric *läppɜ (compare Northern Sami leahppi, Lule Sami sliehppá, Komi-Zyrian лапӧд (lapöd), Udmurt липыны (ľipyny), Northern Mansi [script needed] (lēp-), Hungarian lep).

parole.significato: the steam that rises from the sauna stove (kiuas) or the heat of the sauna
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *leülü (compare Estonian leil), from Proto-Finno-Ugric *lewle (“spirit, soul”) (compare Northern Sami lievla, Komi-Permyak лов (lov), Udmurt лул (lul), Northern Khanty ԓыԓ (łył), Hungarian lélek (“soul, ghost”)).

parole.significato: to be able to, can do
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *mahtadak (compare Estonian mahtuma), from Proto-Finno-Ugric *mačta- (compare Erzya and Moksha маштомс (maštoms), Eastern Mari мошташ (moštaš)).

parole.significato: nectar (sweet liquid secreted by flowers to attract pollinating insects and birds)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *meci (“honey”) (compare Estonian mesi), from Proto-Finno-Ugric *mete (compare Erzya медь (meď), Udmurt му (mu), Hungarian méz), which is probably borrowed from Proto-Indo-European *médʰu (whence English mead), or more specifically from Pre-Proto-Indo-Iranian. In the sense “honey”,

parole.significato: other, another
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *muu (compare Estonian muu), from Proto-Finno-Ugric *mu (compare Northern Sami nubbi, Northern Mansi мо̄т (mōt), Hungarian más).

parole.significato: also, too, likewise, as well
parole.testo: From myö- (“rear, beyond”) + -s (s-lative singular), from Proto-Finnic *möö-, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *müŋä (“rear, beyond”) (compare Erzya мей (mej, “reverse (side)”), мейле (mejle, “later”)). For a similar semantic development, see Hungarian meg (“and, plus”).

parole.significato: hill (a relatively large, usually rounded elevation of earth; generally larger than kukkula (“hill, hillock”) and small…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *mäki (compare Estonian mägi), from Proto-Finno-Ugric *mäke (compare Eastern Khanty мӱг (müg)). First attested in 1303 (in the place name Rænthæmækj, modern Räntämäki).

parole.significato: woman (adult female human being)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *nainën, derived from Proto-Finno-Ugric *näxe-; nai- + -nen. Attested since the time of Mikael Agricola (output c. 1543–1552), but vaimo was the more common word for “woman” in the oldest literary Finnish texts.

parole.significato: four
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *neljä (compare Estonian neli), from Proto-Finno-Ugric *neljä (compare Northern Sami njeallje, Erzya ниле (nile), Northern Mansi нила (nila), Hungarian négy).

parole.significato: phloem (vascular tissue in land plants primarily responsible for the distribution of sugars and nutrients)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *nila, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *ńila. Cognate with Karelian nila, Veps nila, Lule Sami njalle, Erzya нола (nola, “juice”), Northern Khanty ньел (n’jel) and Northern Mansi няль (nâlʹ).

parole.significato: witch (person who uses magic)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *noita (“shaman”) (compare Estonian nõid), from Proto-Finno-Ugric *nojta (compare Northern Sami noaidi (“shaman”)).

parole.significato: lawn, grass (low, dense cover of grass plants; area of land with such a cover)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *nurmi, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *ńurme. Related to Estonian nurm, Karelian nurmi, Livonian nuŗm, Veps norm, Votic nurmi, Skolt Sami njormm, Northern Khanty [script needed] (ńurəm) and Northern Mansi ню̄рым (nû̄rym).

parole.significato: to skin, flay, fleece (remove the skin of an animal)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *nülkedäk, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *ńülke-. Cognate with Erzya нельгемс (neľgems, “to take away”).

parole.significato: shoulder (part of the human torso forming a relatively horizontal surface running away from the neck)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *olka, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *wolka; cognate with Hungarian váll.

parole.significato: synonym of ontelo
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *onci, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *omte (“cavity”) or *oŋte. Cognate with Veps onduz, Erzya ундо (undo, “hole, cavity, hollow”) and Hungarian odú (“haunt, animal hole”).

parole.significato: to learn
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *oppidak (compare Estonian õppima), from Proto-Finno-Ugric *woppe-(j-) (“to see, inspect”) (compare Northern Khanty вопиты (wopity, “to visit; to stalk”), Eastern Mansi [script needed] (wopj-)). Originally meant “to go look, check, examine (a trap, etc.)” as part of hunting vocabul

parole.significato: thorn (sharp protective spine of a plant)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *ora, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *ora (compare Inari Sami oari, Erzya уро (uro), Moksha ура (ura) and Hungarian ár), borrowed from Proto-Indo-Iranian *Hā́raH (compare Sanskrit आरा (ā́rā)), from Proto-Indo-European *h₁ólos (compare Old Norse alr, English awl).

parole.significato: part (fraction of a whole)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *osa (compare Estonian osa), from Proto-Finno-Ugric *ońća (compare Northern Sami oažži and possibly Hungarian ágyék), borrowed from Proto-Indo-Iranian *Hónćos (later *Hánćas, compare Sanskrit अंश (aṃśa)).

parole.significato: to buy, purchase
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *ostadak (compare Estonian ostma), derived from Proto-Finno-Ugric *wosa (compare Komi-Zyrian вуз (vuz, “tax”)) with -taa; in turn, the root might possibly be borrowed from Proto-Indo-Iranian *wasaH. * (to buy, believe, accept (a story, etc.)): Semantic loan from Swedish köpa, perha

parole.significato: to hit, strike, get [with illative] (a spot, target)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *osudak, probably from Proto-Finno-Ugric *ońćo- (“to get”). Probably ultimately equivalent to osa- + -ua. Compare sattua (“to hit, strike, touch”).

parole.significato: to burst
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *pak'ahtudak, derived from Proto-Finno-Ugric *pëkka- (“to burst”). Compare Hungarian fakad (“to spring, burst”).

parole.significato: beam (long, usually round piece of timber for hanging goods for storage, historically specifically one used to dry shea…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *parci, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *pärtä. Related to Estonian pars, Karelian parsi, Livonian parž, Veps parzʹ and Votic parsi, and further Eastern Mari пырдыж (pyrdyž, “wall”), Udmurt борд (bord, “wall”) and Northern Mansi па̄рт (pārt, “board”).

parole.significato: shit, crap, turd (excrement)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *paska (compare Estonian pask), from Proto-Finno-Ugric *pućka (compare Northern Sami baika, Erzya пскиземс (pskizems, “to have diarrhea”), Eastern Mari пушкедаш (puškedaš, “to defecate”), Hungarian fos). The development of the initial vowel from Uralic to Finnic appears to have bee

parole.significato: dam, dyke/dike (structure placed across a flowing body of water to stop the flow or a part of it)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *pato (compare Veps pado), from Proto-Finno-Ugric *pada-w (compare Erzya падо (pado), Hungarian fal).

parole.significato: rowan, mountain ash (Sorbus aucuparia)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *pihlaga (compare Estonian pihlakas, Ingrian pihlaja), from Proto-Finno-Ugric *pićlä (compare Erzya пизёл (piźol), Eastern Mari пызле (pyzĺe), Komi-Zyrian пелысь (pelyś), Northern Khanty писяр (pisjar)).

parole.significato: thorn, prong, tooth or similar element e.g. in a plant, a saw or a rake
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *pii (“tooth”), from Proto-Finno-Ugric *piŋe (“tooth”). Cognates include Ingrian pii (“spike”), Erzya пей (pej, “tooth”) and Hungarian fog (“tooth”).

parole.significato: cultured milk, sour milk, fermented milk, soured milk, (cultured) buttermilk (fermented dairy product produced from cow…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *piimä (“milk”) (cognate with Estonian piim (“milk”), Votic piime (“milk”)), from Proto-Finno-Ugric *pejmä, probably a loanword from Late Proto-Indo-European *péyh₂-men- (specifically Pre-Proto-Indo-Iranian), reflected as Proto-Indo-Iranian *páyHmā (“milk”), from Proto-Indo-Europea

parole.significato: twilight (period between daylight and darkness)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *puktëk, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *pukta- (“to shoo”), the semantic development is likely "to shoo" > "to wake (someone) up" > "time of waking up" > "dawn" > "twilight". Compare Erzya пувтамс (puvtams, “to wake (someone) up”).

parole.significato: to put on, don (clothes; often with päälle)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *pukëdak (compare Livonian pu’ggõ), possibly from Proto-Finno-Ugric *puke-.

parole.significato: The color red.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *puna, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *puna (“color, hair”). Cognate with Erzya пона (pona, “hair”).

parole.significato: to ram, push
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *puskëdak, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *puske-.

parole.significato: head (part of a body)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *pää (compare Estonian pea, Veps pä), from Proto-Finno-Ugric *päŋe (compare Erzya пе (pe), Komi-Zyrian пом (pom), Northern Mansi пуӈк (puňk), Hungarian fej, fő).

parole.significato: swallow, martin (bird of the family Hirundinidae)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *pääskü, perhaps from Proto-Finno-Ugric *päčkɜ and/or simply onomatopoeic. Cognates include Karelian piäčkyni, Estonian pääsuke, pääsu, Ingrian pääsky, Livonian pešlinki, Veps päskheińe, Votic pääsko, Erzya пезьгун (peźgun), пезьгата (peźgata), Udmurt пӧськы (pöśky) and Hungarian f

parole.significato: sermon (religious discourse)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *sarna (compare Veps sarn), possibly from Proto-Finno-Ugric *ćarńa (“incantation, speech”) (compare Komi-Zyrian сёрни (śorńi)).

parole.significato: pole (long and slender piece of metal or especially wood, used for various construction or support purposes)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *salko, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *śëlkaw, a loan from an early descendant of Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰalgʰ- (“slat”). Finno-Ugric cognates include Karelian šalko, Northern Sami čuolggu (“lever, crowbar”), Erzya сялго (śalgo, “stick”), Hungarian szál (“fiber”), Northern Mansi са̄гла (sā

parole.significato: horn (growth of keratin that protrudes from the head of certain animals)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *sarvi (compare Estonian sarv), from Proto-Finno-Ugric *śarwe (compare Erzya сюро (śuro) and Hungarian szarv), borrowed from Proto-Indo-Iranian *ćr̥Hwa- (compare Avestan 𐬯𐬭𐬏 (srū, “horn, claw, talon”), 𐬯𐬭𐬎𐬎𐬁 (sruuā, “horn”)), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *ḱerh₂-. Doublet of

parole.significato: hundred
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *sata (compare Estonian sada), from Proto-Finno-Ugric *śëta (“hundred”) (compare Erzya сядо (śado), Northern Mansi са̄т (sāt), Hungarian száz), borrowed from Proto-Indo-Iranian *ćatám (compare Avestan 𐬯𐬀𐬙𐬀 (sata), Sanskrit शत (śatá)), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *ḱm̥tóm.

parole.significato: to bind, tie, fasten
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *sitodak (compare Estonian siduma, Veps sidoda), from Proto-Finno-Ugric *sita- (compare Erzya содомс (sodoms)). * (to bind, oblige): Likely a semantic loan from other languages, ultimately a semantic loan from Latin obligō.

parole.significato: to sound (to make a musical sound)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *soidak, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *śoje- (compare Northern Sami čuodjat, Hungarian zaj).

parole.significato: Any bird of the genus Aythya including scaups, pochards, canvasbacks etc.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *sotka, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *śoδka.

parole.significato: to cram, stuff, crowd (press, force, or drive, particularly in filling, or in thrusting one thing into another)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *survodak, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *śurwa-.

parole.significato: autumn, fall (season of the year)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *süksü, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *sükśe. Cognates include Estonian sügis, Karelian šygyžy, Northern Sami čakča, Erzya сёксь (śokś), Hungarian ősz.

parole.significato: deep
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *cüvä (compare Estonian süva), probably from Proto-Finno-Ugric *tiwä (compare e.g. Northern Sami davvi (“north”), Eastern Mari тӱнӧ (tünö)).

parole.significato: to cut into splinters
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *sälidäk, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *śälä-, *ćälä-.

parole.significato: to break, shatter, smash (cause to break into two or more pieces)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *särkedäk (compare Votic särčiä), from Proto-Finno-Ugric *ćärke- (compare Lule Sami tjiergav, Northern Mansi [script needed] (saɣr-) and possibly Hungarian sért (“to injure”), although the last of these would be irregular).

parole.significato: roach (Rutilus rutilus, fish)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *särki (compare Estonian särg), from Proto-Finno-Ugric *särke (compare Erzya сэрьге (sëŕge)).

parole.significato: ide, Leuciscus idus
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *säünä-, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *säwnä. Derived with various suffixes since; säyne contains -e. Cognates include Estonian säinas, Northern Sami seavnnját, Moksha сеня (senä) and Hungarian őn.

parole.significato: weather
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *sää (compare Karelian seä, siä, šiä, Veps sä, Votic sää), from Proto-Finno-Ugric *säŋe (“air”) (compare Hungarian ég (“sky”) and Komi-Zyrian сынӧд (synöd, “warm air”)).

parole.significato: osprey (Pandion haliaetus)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *säksi, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *śäkće ~ *śäkśe.

parole.significato: to do, perform, execute, carry out
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *tektäk (compare Estonian tegema, Veps tehta), from Proto-Finno-Ugric *teke- (compare Northern Sami dahkat, Erzya теемс (tejems), Hungarian tesz; see the Proto-Uralic entry for more).

parole.significato: calm, still, tranquil, serene
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *tüüni, derived from Proto-Finno-Ugric *tiwä (compare Northern Khanty тевән (tjewən)). Compare also syvä (< *tiwä).

parole.significato: leftover, leavings, residue (whatever remains when something - usually the useful part - has been removed; food left ov…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *täkteh, probably from Proto-Finno-Ugric *täktä (whence Proto-Samic *tāktē).

parole.significato: curtain, drape
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *uudin, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *owdeme. Related to Eastern Khanty ө̆ԓәп (ø̆łəp) and Eastern Mansi амыл (amyl). Mostly displaced by verho.

parole.significato: new
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *uuci (compare Estonian uus), from Proto-Finno-Ugric *wuďe (compare Northern Sami ođas, Erzya and Moksha од (od), Eastern Mari and Western Mari у (u), Komi-Zyrian выль (vyľ), Hungarian új). The vowel was irregularly lengthened possibly as a result of the lost initial *w-.

parole.significato: to sink [with illative ‘in’] (something heavier than water)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *vajot'ak (compare Estonian vajuma, Ingrian vajota, Karelian vajota, Livonian va’jjõ, Veps vajuda and Votic vajoota (Mati)), from Proto-Finno-Ugric *waja- (compare Northern Sami vuodjut, Erzya and Moksha ваямс (vajäms), Udmurt выйыны (vyjyny), Northern Mansi [script needed] (uj-) a

parole.significato: haven (protected harbour or anchorage for small boats)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *valkama, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *wëlka- (“to descend, to go down”). Compare Erzya валгомс (valgoms, “to alight”).

parole.significato: white, (very) light (with a white or off-white color)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *valkëda (compare Estonian valge, Karelian valkie /valgie), from Proto-Finno-Ugric *wëlketa (compare Northern Sami vielgat, Erzya валдо (valdo), Eastern Mari волгыдо (volgydo)), from *wëlke (“light”) (compare Hungarian világ).

parole.significato: to whisk, whip
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *vackat'ak (compare Karelian vatkata), from Proto-Finno-Ugric *wačka- (compare Erzya вачкамс (vačkams, “to pile up”), вачкодемс (vačkodems, “to stick”), Eastern Mari вӱчкалташ (vüčkaltaš, “to pat on the back”) and possibly Eastern Khanty [Term?] (“to spread water with one's hand”))

parole.significato: knife (tool, weapon)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *väicci, possibly from Proto-Finno-Ugric *wäŋćɜ (compare Hungarian vés (“chisel”)).

parole.significato: blood (liquid flowing in human and animal bodies)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *veri (compare Estonian veri, Livonian ve’r), from Proto-Finno-Ugric *were (compare Northern Sami varra, Erzya верь (veŕ), Eastern Mari вӱр (vür), Udmurt вир (vir), Hungarian vér).

parole.significato: to pull, drag, draw (to apply a pulling force)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *vetädäk, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *wetä- (compare Erzya ветямс (veťams), Hungarian vezet). Semantic development Most senses are straightforward from the original “to pull, drag, draw”. * (to wind (up) a mechanism): Often done by pulling on a part, a string, etc. * (to flush): Older

parole.significato: last, past (most recent, last so far)
parole.testo: Derived from Proto-Finnic *viimä- (whence also viimeinen (“last”)), from Proto-Finno-Ugric *wiŋe-mä (same root *wiŋe as in viipyä (“to stay”)). The final vowel may be by analogy with viimein, viimeinen (note however the dialectal viimi, also found in Karelian viimi).

parole.significato: butter
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *voi (compare Estonian või), from Proto-Finno-Ugric *waje (compare Northern Sami vuodja, Erzya ой (oj), Western Mari ӱ (ü), Udmurt вӧй (vöj), Hungarian vaj).

parole.significato: bed (prepared spot in which to spend the night; one's place of sleep or rest)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *voodëk ~ *voodëh, possibly equivalent to vuota (“hide”) + -e. A native derivation from Proto-Finno-Ugric *aďe- (“to set the bed”) has also been proposed. Cognate with Estonian voodi.

parole.significato: wagtail (any bird of the family Motacillidae, which includes wagtails and pipits)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *västärikko (compare Estonian västrik, Ingrian väistärikko, Karelian päistärikkö, väistärikkö, Votic vässo), possibly from Proto-Finno-Ugric (compare Northern Sami beštor, Erzya уськерей (uśkerej), Southern Khanty вәрться̈к (wərt’sjäk), Eastern Mansi уртшых (urtšyh)), but probably

parole.significato: core, kernel, nucleus, the central part of something
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *üdin (“bone marrow”) (compare Estonian üdi, Karelian yjin), from Proto-Finno-Ugric *wideme ~ *wüdeme ~ *wädeme (“bone marrow”) (compare Northern Sami ađa (“(bone with) marrow”), Erzya удем (udem, “marrow; intellect”), Eastern Mari вем (vem, “marrow”), Hungarian velő (“marrow”)).

parole.significato: sound; noise (sound as a perceived or physical phenomenon; the sound emitted by something)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *ääni (compare Veps änʹ), from Proto-Finno-Ugric *äne (compare Northern Sami jietna, Hungarian ének). * (vote): Semantic loan from Swedish röst.
